boston air pollution control commission
steven p. cohen executive director
617 227-4890 722-4100
September 28, 1975
Ms. Martha Goldsmith
Cffice of Community Development
Room 703, City Hall
Boston, Massachusetts 02201
Dear Ms. Goldsmith:
The Boston Air Pollution Control Commission has reviewed the Draft Environmental Impact Statement for the Clearence of Unsafe Buildings - Community Development Block Grant Program and is in full support of the program. The EIS was generally well prepared, and was quite comprehensive and honest in its assessment of the impacts. We were quite pleased to see that contract provisions are being made to limit the impacts from fugitive dust and excessive noise.
We have a few questions and comments on the draft statement however. They are as follows:
Page 5: Public Safety and Health
"Increased accident rotential to workmen and bystanders" - should be under heading "Fotentially Adverse"
"Strict enforcement of the State Building Code regarding public safety during demolition"
- should be under heading "Measures to Minimize Harm"
Page 6: Economic - Beneficial
"__ man years of employment in demolition operations and extermination"
- blank should be filled in
Social - Beneficial
- encourage what?
Fage 38: "Altogether, almost 9,800 people lived in <u>Hyde Square</u> in 1970" - should be changed to Egleston Square
Page 87: Inadequate information is given as to why "approved sanitary landfill" disposal will be $400-800 more expensive than the alternatives.
Page 90: City Noise Regulations
- The BAPCC Regulations are slightly misinterpreted here. The noise level readings shall be taken at the affected
